description: Blueprint 16.1 - the UNIVERSAL CORE. Identical everywhere, NOT configurable. A hospital profile may TIGHTEN a safety floor and may never loosen one. This asymmetry is checked at profile load; an invalid profile is rejected with a named violation rather than partially applied.
three_laws: Law 3 - attention only ratchets up; every de-escalation is a human act.

protocol_floors_minutes._comment: Universal reassessment intervals for WAITING patients. The single most important external anchor in the design (Blueprint 7.3). The engine may SHORTEN these; nobody may lengthen them. Level 1 is continuous - represented as 0.
protocol_floors_minutes.citation_text: Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale mandatory reassessment intervals for waiting patients: level 1 continuous, level 2 every 15 minutes, level 3 every 30, level 4 every 60, level 5 every 120.

max_wait_to_first_assessment_minutes._comment: Blueprint 7.3 - used as the starvation-guard bound in constraint C2. If the optimiser cannot keep every patient inside their band's bound, it declares insufficiency rather than reordering.

blind_uncertainty.note: Blueprint 7.4: tighter than any CTAS interval except continuous. A patient who cannot be assessed is structurally impossible to lose for more than ten minutes.

conflicted_uncertainty.note: Blueprint 10.3: clock to the conflict floor.

undetermined_envelope.note: Blueprint complexity 4 fallback: if the envelope cannot be determined, apply the most conservative thresholds across all envelopes and floor the clock at 10 minutes.

conformal.note: Blueprint 7.4 and invariant I10: alpha may be LOWERED by a hospital (more conservative, wider sets, more escalation) and never raised above the ceiling.

insufficient_calibration_fallback.behaviour: alpha defaults to its most conservative permitted value and the set defaults to {point estimate, one level more acute}

uncertainty.note: Blueprint 7.4: weighted completeness <0.60 -> THIN; ANY critical-1 field absent -> THIN regardless of the score. The second clause is the important one - a single absent critical field cannot be outvoted by a high overall completeness score.

worklist.note: Blueprint 7.4: K = clamp(round(capacity), 1, 5), default 3. Above 5 the list stops being a worklist and becomes an alarm stream (the documented Epic failure mode [S4]).

hard_class_names.R: RED FLAG ACTIVE - a deterministic L2 rule is firing and unactioned
hard_class_names.E: EXPIRED - TTL elapsed and no reassessment recorded
hard_class_names.B: BLIND - uncertainty class BLIND, patient cannot be assessed

queue.time_pressure_gamma_note: Blueprint 11.2: gamma > 1. The exponent is the whole idea - priority rises SUPERLINEARLY as a clock approaches expiry, so a patient at 90% of their clock outranks one at 45% by much more than 2x. This is what converts 'time waiting' from a fairness term into a safety term.
queue.hysteresis_note: Blueprint 7.4: 5% of harm score. Stops patients oscillating across a rank boundary when their scores are effectively tied.
queue.resource_note: Constraint C3: resource state may break ties within an epsilon band and may inform routing. It may never move a patient down by more than k positions, never reduce an acted acuity, and never lengthen a clock.

STRAINED.note: The mortality-associated ED occupancy threshold identified in a 103,196-visit study; above it, 10-day mortality odds rose for non-critical patients. Our mode change is anchored to a measured harm inflection rather than a round number.

MCI.entry: load >= 6x normal OR simultaneous critical arrivals exceeding resus capacity
MCI.note: The system declares itself out of protocol. Per-patient TTL mathematics is stated to be no longer meaningful at that scale.

mode_asymmetry.note: Blueprint 9.3 / 27: the system may auto-ENTER a more vigilant mode - consistent with the ratchet - but only a HUMAN may LEAVE one. Vigilance is free to increase itself and never free to decrease itself.

degradation_note: Blueprint 13.2: every rung is announced by a persistent banner, logged as a mode-change event, and produces clocks AT LEAST AS SHORT as the rung above it (invariant I5). The system degrades upward into vigilance, never downward into silence.

rules.P1: A recommendation whose reassuring evidence rests only on {Pt, Att, Unk} can never reach uncertainty class CLEAR.
rules.P2: Der values are never fed back as inputs. The model does not consume its own output.
rules.P3: RecProvisional may increase risk or shorten a clock. It may never decrease risk, lengthen a clock, or lower an acted acuity level.

provenance_lattice.unknown_note: Blueprint 8.5: provenance unknown is treated as Pt, the least trusted plausible class - never the most.

half_lives_minutes._comment: Blueprint 8.6. Beyond its half-life a value's weight decays toward UNKNOWN - which raises uncertainty and shortens the clock - and NEVER toward normal. Past 2x half-life the value becomes Absent and generates a re-measure task.
half_lives_minutes._onset_note: The onset clock NEVER expires - it counts up, and it belongs to the disease rather than to the queue.

prohibitions: No autonomous de-escalation of any kind.
No autonomous exit from a more vigilant operating mode.
No LLM in the clinical decision path.
No headline accuracy or AUC figure.

audit.note: Blueprint 15.2: the audit record is committed DURABLY BEFORE the recommendation is displayed. The log can never lag the screen. If the audit store is unavailable, clinical decisions are REFUSED, not queued.
audit.retention_note: DPDP Rule 6 requires logs and personal data to be retained for one year unless another law requires otherwise. Configurable floor - may only be RAISED.
